hints.title: Tree Acyclicity and Connectivity Obstacle
hints.text: An undirected graph forms a tree if and only if it is fully connected and contains zero cycles. What strict edge count must hold for n vertices, and how can tracking connectivity catch duplicate paths early?

hints.title: Exact Edge Count and Acyclic Invariant
hints.text: A valid tree with n nodes must have exactly n - 1 edges. If this condition holds, proving that no cycles exist guarantees that all vertices belong to a single connected component.

hints.title: Disjoint Set Cycle Detection Procedure
hints.text: First verify that edge count equals n - 1. If not, return false. Initialize disjoint sets for each vertex. For each edge, look up the canonical representative of both vertices. If the representatives match, a cycle is present, so return false. Otherwise, link the representatives together. Return true if all edges process without cycle detection.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Checking edge count takes O(1); processing n - 1 edges with path compression runs in near-linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: DFS/BFS cycle detection without checking edge count incurs unnecessary recursion overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Parent array requires O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: First asserting that edge count must equal n - 1 before testing acyclicity.
